messages:
maria: Heads-up — Im seeing a burst of concurrent uploads in the sample app when connectivity is restored. OkHttp queues and then fires ~20 calls at once; auth interceptor ends up doing multiple refreshes.

aj: That usually means refresh isn't single-flight + retryOnConnectionFailure is letting transient errors retry and then pile. Which okhttp + retrofit versions?

maria: okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0, kotlin coroutines adapter. snippet from the client:

```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 20 })
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```

maria: When the OS re-enables network (WorkManager constraints lifted) we see log spikes: many "refreshing token" lines and 429s.

tim: Another angle: coroutine CallAdapter parity. If worker cancels but adapter doesn't cancel underlying Call properly we might have duplicate inflight attempts. Confirm that your callAdapterFactory uses call.cancel() on coroutine cancellation.

sophia: Also check that token refresh uses a Mutex/Deferred instead of naive synchronized; synchronized can block threads in a coroutine dispatcher and cause more queued work. Example pattern: use an AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>> singleflight.

aj: I prefer this pattern with Mutex + tryLock to avoid blocking threads: with(singleflightMutex) { if (tokenExpired) refresh() } and other callers tryLock + suspend/wait for result.

maria: Repro logs (trimmed):

```
2026-03-15 09:12:01 UploadWorker: network ready, starting batch n=18
2026-03-15 09:12:01 AuthInterceptor: token expired, start refresh
2026-03-15 09:12:01 AuthInterceptor: token expired, start refresh
2026-03-15 09:12:02 Retrofit: 401 -> trigger refresh
2026-03-15 09:12:02 Retrofit: 429 rate limited
```

maria: Each call logs its own refresh attempt. Not deduped.

aj: Quick mitigation: reduce maxRequestsPerHost to something small in samples (4 or 6), set retryOnConnectionFailure(false), and debounce token refresh with a Coroutine Mutex or Deferred singleflight. Also, move heavy uploads into a single UploadCoordinator that drains a bounded queue.

tim: For the sample app we should add an integration test that simulates offline -> online and asserts only one refresh network call per token expiry. Helps prevent regressions.

sophia: PR idea: change sample auth interceptor to use this pattern, reduce dispatcher concurrency, and update worker to use ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP or an aggregator worker. I'll open a PR.

ci-bot: build: PR 987 (sampleapp/oauth-singleflight)  tests queued

maria: Thanks — if you land the singleflight + smaller dispatcher I'll run on Pixel 7 + emulator and try flappy-network toggles. Also let's add a small debug metric: dispatcher.queuedCalls and activeCalls counts to the console logs for a short window so we can correlate.

aj: Agreed. Also call out cancellation semantics in the README section for Android SDK (coroutine adapter behavior). We had at least one customer confused by cancellation not always propagating.

sophia: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/987 — includes tests and notes.

maria: Great. I'll smoke test and report results. :thumbsup:
